text: dsh-memory-search 是面向 DSH agent 的长期记忆检索插件，可在支持插件工具和系统提示扩展的 DSH 客户端中使用。它递归索引配置目录中的 Markdown 笔记，使用 SQLite FTS5 关键词检索，并可选用本地 embedding 做语义检索，再融合结果。主要功能包括主动调用 memory_search 查询原文片段、每轮自动把相关笔记加入系统提示、按文件与会话映射筛选召回范围，以及增量同步变更笔记。适合希望让 agent 查找个人笔记和历史记录的用户。无需 API key；向量检索需本地 GGUF 模型。

dsh-memory-search indexes Markdown notes for DSH agents with SQLite FTS5 and optional local embeddings. It returns source passages through memory_search, adds relevant notes to each system prompt, and refreshes the index when notes change. No API key is needed; vector search uses a local GGUF model.
想让 DSH agent 能从我写的 Markdown 笔记里找回以前记录的内容。
怎样让每轮对话自动带上相关的旧笔记作为上下文？
我想用关键词和本地向量一起搜索个人知识库。
能不能让 agent 搜索记忆时返回原文和文件位置？
笔记更新后怎样只重新索引改过的 Markdown 文件？
我想让不同会话只能检索允许访问的笔记级别。
How can my DSH agent search my Markdown notes for something I mentioned before?
I want relevant notes automatically added to each turn’s system context.
Markdown 笔记混合检索：递归索引配置目录中的笔记，以 SQLite FTS5 关键词和可选本地向量分别召回，再融合排名。
主动记忆查询：agent 调用 memory_search 并提供查询词，工具返回相关原文片段、文件路径和起始行号。
每轮自动召回：收到用户消息后按其文本检索记忆，并把命中片段加入系统提示上下文，供 agent 在当前回复中参考。
增量笔记同步：后台定时重新扫描语料，根据文件修改时间和大小更新索引，并清理已删除文件的索引记录。

dsh-memory-search README · dsh-memory-search：[English](README.en.md) | 简体中文

给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（dsh）用的**长期记忆检索**插件。

把一堆 markdown 笔记做成 Agent「想得起来」的记忆：两路召回（本地向量 + 关键词），
每轮自动把相关的旧事带进上下文，Agent 也能自己 `memory_search` 去翻。

> 一个跑得久的 Agent，问题常常不是模型不够聪明，而是**它不记得**。
> 这个插件不训练、不微调，只做一件事：把你自己写的笔记，变成随时查得到的记忆。

dsh-memory-search README · dsh-memory-search：> **同类里更成熟的选择**：[csyangwen/dsh-memory-evolve](https://github.com/csyangwen/dsh-memory-evolve)、[Aik358/dsh-auto-memory](https://github.com/Aik358/dsh-auto-memory)、[FuRongJun-1999/dsh-memory](https://github.com/FuRongJun-1999/dsh-memory) 都比这份成熟，要装先看它们。
> 我们这份留着的理由：它是**我们自己线上记忆检索的抽出版**——两路召回（本地向量 + 关键词）和密级过滤都是跑过的那套，
> 自检自带语料、不用先接上你的数据，索引删了也能从 `.md` 重建。
> 功能面比上面几个窄，选之前先比一比。

- 笔记你随时能打开改，改完索引自己跟上（按 mtime/size 增量重切，只动改过的那篇）
- 备份、diff、git 版本化都是现成的
- 索引删了随时重建 —— 笔记是唯一的真相来源

text:
dsh-memory-search README · 特性：- **混合召回**：SQLite FTS5 关键词 + 本地 embedding 向量，RRF 融合 —— 「原话」和「意思」各管一半。
  中文按重叠 bigram 在应用层切词，**不用编译任何 SQLite 扩展**。
- **零 API 花费**：向量模型跑在本地（`node-llama-cpp`，CPU 就行）。
- **不装模型也能用**：`modelPath` 留空就只跑关键词那一路，一条依赖都不用多。
- **两个出口**：`memory_search` 工具（Agent 主动查）+ 每轮自动召回（塞进系统提示，**不进对话记录**）。
- **可选密级**：同一堆语料里，群聊只可能召回 public，私事只在主人会话里出现。
- **切块规范有闸**：改切块规则不会偷偷把全库向量重算一遍，要你显式点头。

dsh-memory-search README · 安装：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:JackZo400/dsh-memory-search
```

装完按下面的「配置」改一遍，再重启对应 profile。

**环境要求**：Node **≥ 22.5**（用的是内置 `node:sqlite`；实测 22.22 直接可用，会打一条
`ExperimentalWarning`，属正常）。想开向量检索才需要装 `node-llama-cpp` 并自己下一个 GGUF 模型
—— 它列在 `optionalDependencies` 里，装不上也不影响关键词检索。

dsh-memory-search README · 配置：配置写在你的 profile patch 里（bundle patch 的 `insert` 段）：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: memory-search
      name: dsh-memory-search
      config:

几个容易踩的点：

- **`roots` 不配就是空索引**，日志会提醒你。
- **`modelPath` 留空**时插件只建关键词索引，`embedding.enabled` 开着也白开（不会报错）。
- **`queryInstruction`**：默认值是给 Qwen3-Embedding 用的指令前缀（它 instruction-aware，
  检索质量吃这个前缀）。**换别的嵌入模型（bge-m3、nomic 之类）建议在配置里显式清空**，
  不然前缀会污染语义。
- **换嵌入模型要删掉索引库重建** —— 向量维度不同，旧向量没法复用（代码会检测到维度不匹配，
  直接放弃语义那一路，不会给你算出垃圾结果）。

dsh-memory-search README · 配置（语料怎么放）：没有固定结构，递归收 `.md`，两个建议：

1. **一条一事**（一个 bullet 一件事、段落之间空行）。切块是按「空行 / 列表项 / 标题」
   这些边界走的 —— 相邻的两件事被塞进同一块，检索精度会掉。
2. **事实文件别混进大量流水账**。语料里「日记里我正在讨论这件事」的段落会字面上更像查询，
   把真正的事实挤出前排。插件给 `public.md` / `personal.md` / `secret.md` 这类文件加了
   1.5 倍来源权重、给 `carryover/` 目录降了权，但语料结构还是你自己最清楚。

dsh-memory-search README · 配置（密级，可选）：判据是**文件名**（放在哪个目录下都行）：

| 文件名 | 密级 | 谁能召回 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public.md` | `public` | 所有会话 |
| `personal.md` | `personal` | 只有 owner 会话 |
| `secret.md` | `secret` | 只有 owner 会话 |
| 其它任何文件 | `personal`（保守） | 只有 owner 会话 |

「谁是 owner」由可选的**通道映射**决定 —— 一个 JSON，把会话 key 映射到 session id：

```json
{ "c2c:1A2B3C": { "sessionId": "8f0c…" }, "group:123456": { "sessionId": "ab12…" } }
```

dsh-memory-search README · 配置（密级，可选）：配上 `sessionMap` 之后：`group:`/`grp:` 开头的 key 判成 `group`（只给 public）、
在 `ownerIds` 里的判成 `owner`（全给）、其余判成 `guest`（只给 public）。
**判不出通道时不召回**（fail closed）—— 宁可少给，不可漏私事。

**不配 `sessionMap` 就不做任何过滤**，所有会话都当 owner —— 单人使用（不接群）的时候，
这才是你想要的默认。

dsh-memory-search README · 工作原理：```
markdown 语料 ──scan──▶ 切块（按条目边界）──▶ SQLite
                                              ├── chunks（正文 + 向量 BLOB）
                                              └── chunks_fts（bigram token）
查询 ──┬── FTS5 MATCH ──▶ bm25 排名 ─┐

dsh-memory-search README · 工作原理：- **RRF 融合**：不比较两路的分数（bm25 和余弦根本不是一个量纲），只比名次。
- **切块**：按空行 / 列表项 / markdown 标题切，条目超长才按长度硬切；保留起始行号，方便回原文。
- **增量**：每个文件记 mtime + size，只重切变过的；删掉的文件从索引里忘掉。
- **切块规范闸**：切块规则变了（`CHUNK_SIG`），默认**只记账不重切** ——
  要重切得设 `acceptSpecChange: true`（那一下会把全部向量重算）。
- **两个出口**：`memory_search` 工具返回原文片段 + 出处（不是摘要）；
  自动召回挂在 `system-prompt/assemble` 上，往系统提示里加一段 `memory-search`，
  **不写进对话记录**，所以不会污染上下文历史。

dsh-memory-search README · 测试：```bash
node test/selftest.mjs         # 切块 / 分词 / 索引 / 检索（临时语料，无外部依赖）
node test/plugin-selftest.mjs  # 插件契约：工具注册、系统提示段、服务暴露、密级
node test/spec-guard.mjs       # 切块规范闸：改了规则不许偷偷重切
npm test                       # 上面三个一起

`test/recall-eval.mjs` 是**评测脚手架**，不是自检 —— 它对着你自己的索引库跑一批
「问句 → 期望命中的片段/文件」的题，报告 top-1 / top-3 / top-5 命中率：

```bash
node test/recall-eval.mjs --db .dsh-memory/index.db --corpus ./memory
```

题目要按你自己的语料改（文件头部有示例）。**这是这个插件最该动的地方** ——
召回质量跟语料结构强相关，我给的默认权重只在一类语料上验证过。

dsh-memory-search README · 已知局限：- **切块规则是启发式的**（空行/列表/标题），对「一大段长文」的笔记不友好。
- **来源权重是硬编码的三条**，按文件名/目录匹配。语料结构差异大的话，得改 `src/recall.js`。
- **向量检索是全量扫描**（几百到几千块是毫秒级，上万块就该上专门的向量库了）。
- **中文分词只做 bigram**，没有词表 —— 专有名词查得准，语法层面的理解不做。
- **嵌入模型只在 Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B 上验证过**，换模型请留意 `queryInstruction` 和维度。

dsh-memory-search README · dsh-memory-search：[简体中文](README.md) | English

A **long-term memory search** plugin for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).

It turns a pile of markdown notes into memory an agent can actually recall:
two recall paths (local vectors + keywords), relevant old notes pulled into the
context every turn, and a `memory_search` tool the agent can dig through itself.

dsh-memory-search README · dsh-memory-search：> A long-running agent's problem is usually not that the model is not smart
> enough, but that **it does not remember**.
> This plugin does not train and does not fine-tune. It does one thing: turns the
> notes you wrote yourself into memory you can look up at any time.

dsh-memory-search README · dsh-memory-search：> **More mature options in the same space**: [csyangwen/dsh-memory-evolve](https://github.com/csyangwen/dsh-memory-evolve),
> [Aik358/dsh-auto-memory](https://github.com/Aik358/dsh-auto-memory) and
> [FuRongJun-1999/dsh-memory](https://github.com/FuRongJun-1999/dsh-memory) are all more mature than this
> one; look at them first if you are choosing.
> Why we keep this one: it is **the memory-search part extracted from our own production setup** - the two
> recall paths (local vectors + keywords) and the access-level filter are the ones that actually ran, its
> self-tests bring their own corpus so you do not have to wire up your data first, and a deleted index is
> rebuilt from the `.md` files.
> Its feature set is narrower than theirs, so compare before you pick.

dsh-memory-search README · Why you need it (markdown as the corpus)：Memory lives in `.md` files on disk; the database is only an **index**:

- You can open and edit a note whenever you like, and the index catches up on its
  own (incremental re-chunking by mtime/size, touching only the note that changed)
- Backup, diff and git versioning all come for free
- Delete the index and rebuild it any time — your notes are the single source of truth

text:
dsh-memory-search README · Features：- **Hybrid recall**: SQLite FTS5 keywords + local embedding vectors, fused with
  RRF — the literal words and the meaning each carry half the load. Chinese is
  tokenized at the application layer as overlapping bigrams, so **no SQLite
  extension has to be compiled**.
- **Zero API cost**: the embedding model runs locally (`node-llama-cpp`, CPU is
  enough).
- **Works without a model**: leave `modelPath` empty and only the keyword path
  runs, with not one extra dependency.
- **Two exits**: the `memory_search` tool (the agent asks on purpose) + automatic
  per-turn recall (injected into the system prompt, **never written into the
  conversation log**).
- **Optional access levels**: inside one corpus, a group chat can only ever recall
  public notes, and private matters only surface in the owner's session.
- **A gate on the chunking spec**: changing the chunking rules will not silently
  recompute every vector in the whole library; it needs your explicit approval.

dsh-memory-search README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:JackZo400/dsh-memory-search
```

After installing, go through the "Configuration" section below, then restart the
matching profile.

dsh-memory-search README · Install：**Requirements**: Node **≥ 22.5** (it uses the built-in `node:sqlite`; verified
working on 22.22, which prints one `ExperimentalWarning` — that is normal). Vector
search additionally needs `node-llama-cpp` plus a GGUF model you download yourself
— it is listed under `optionalDependencies`, and failing to install it does not
affect keyword search.

dsh-memory-search README · Configuration：Configuration goes into your profile patch (the `insert` section of the bundle
patch):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: memory-search
      name: dsh-memory-search
      config:

A few things that are easy to trip over:

dsh-memory-search README · Configuration：- **No `roots` means an empty index**, and the log will remind you.
- **With `modelPath` empty** the plugin builds a keyword index only; turning
  `embedding.enabled` on does nothing (and raises no error).
- **`queryInstruction`**: the default is the instruction prefix for
  Qwen3-Embedding (it is instruction-aware, and retrieval quality depends on that
  prefix). **If you switch to another embedding model (bge-m3, nomic and the
  like), clear it explicitly in the config**, or the prefix will pollute the
  semantics.
- **Switching embedding models means deleting the index and rebuilding it** — the
  vector dimensions differ, so old vectors cannot be reused (the code detects the
  dimension mismatch and drops the semantic path outright rather than handing you
  garbage results).

dsh-memory-search README · Configuration (laying out your corpus)：There is no fixed structure; `.md` files are collected recursively. Two
suggestions:

dsh-memory-search README · Configuration (laying out your corpus)：1. **One item per entry** (one bullet per fact, blank lines between paragraphs).
   Chunking follows boundaries like blank lines / list items / headings — push two
   neighbouring facts into the same chunk and retrieval precision drops.
2. **Do not mix a lot of running journal text into your fact files.** A passage
   like "in my diary I was discussing this very thing" is literally closer to the
   query and shoves the real fact out of the top ranks. The plugin gives files such
   as `public.md` / `personal.md` / `secret.md` a 1.5x source weight and
   down-weights the `carryover/` directory, but no one knows your corpus structure
   better than you do.

dsh-memory-search README · Configuration (access levels, optional)：The criterion is the **file name** (the directory it sits in does not matter):

| File name | Level | Who can recall it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public.md` | `public` | all sessions |
| `personal.md` | `personal` | owner sessions only |
| `secret.md` | `secret` | owner sessions only |
| any other file | `personal` (conservative) | owner sessions only |

Who counts as the owner is decided by an optional **channel map** — a JSON that
maps a session key to a session id:

dsh-memory-search README · Configuration (access levels, optional)：```json
{ "c2c:1A2B3C": { "sessionId": "8f0c…" }, "group:123456": { "sessionId": "ab12…" } }
```

Once `sessionMap` is configured: keys starting with `group:`/`grp:` are judged
`group` (public only), keys listed in `ownerIds` are judged `owner` (everything),
and the rest are judged `guest` (public only). **When the channel cannot be
determined, nothing is recalled** (fail closed) — better to hand out too little
than to leak something private.

dsh-memory-search README · Configuration (access levels, optional)：**Without `sessionMap` no filtering happens at all** and every session counts as
the owner — for single-user setups (no group chats) that is the default you want.

dsh-memory-search README · How it works：```
markdown 语料 ──scan──▶ 切块（按条目边界）──▶ SQLite
                                              ├── chunks（正文 + 向量 BLOB）
                                              └── chunks_fts（bigram token）
查询 ──┬── FTS5 MATCH ──▶ bm25 排名 ─┐

dsh-memory-search README · How it works：- **RRF fusion**: it never compares the scores of the two paths (bm25 and cosine
  are not even the same unit), only their ranks.
- **Chunking**: split on blank lines / list items / markdown headings; only an
  over-long entry is hard-split by length. Start line numbers are kept so you can
  go back to the source text.
- **Incremental**: mtime + size is recorded per file, so only changed files are
  re-chunked; deleted files are forgotten from the index.
- **Chunking-spec gate**: when the chunking rules change (`CHUNK_SIG`), by default
  it only **records the fact and does not re-chunk** — re-chunking requires
  `acceptSpecChange: true` (and that recomputes every vector).
- **Two exits**: the `memory_search` tool returns raw passages + their source (not
  a summary); automatic recall hooks into `system-prompt/assemble` and adds a
  `memory-search` block to the system prompt, **without writing it into the
  conversation log**, so it does not pollute the context history.

dsh-memory-search README · Tests：```bash
node test/selftest.mjs         # 切块 / 分词 / 索引 / 检索（临时语料，无外部依赖）
node test/plugin-selftest.mjs  # 插件契约：工具注册、系统提示段、服务暴露、密级
node test/spec-guard.mjs       # 切块规范闸：改了规则不许偷偷重切
npm test                       # 上面三个一起

`test/recall-eval.mjs` is an **evaluation harness**, not a self-test — it runs a
batch of "question → passage/file expected to hit" cases against your own index
database and reports top-1 / top-3 / top-5 hit rates:

dsh-memory-search README · Tests：```bash
node test/recall-eval.mjs --db .dsh-memory/index.db --corpus ./memory
```

The cases have to be rewritten for your own corpus (there are examples at the top
of the file). **This is the part of the plugin most worth touching** — recall
quality is tightly coupled to corpus structure, and the default weights I ship were
only validated on one kind of corpus.

dsh-memory-search README · Known limitations：- **The chunking rules are heuristic** (blank lines / lists / headings) and are
  unfriendly to notes written as one long stretch of prose.
- **The source weights are three hard-coded rules**, matched by file name /
  directory. If your corpus structure differs a lot, you have to edit
  `src/recall.js`.
- **Vector search is a full scan** (milliseconds for hundreds to a few thousand
  chunks; at tens of thousands of chunks you should move to a dedicated vector
  store).
- **Chinese tokenization is bigram-only**, with no vocabulary — proper nouns are
  matched precisely, but no syntactic-level understanding is attempted.
- **The embedding model was only validated on Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B**; when you
  switch models, mind `queryInstruction` and the dimensions.
